references.text: Here we find the original ordinance concerning the morning and evening offering, where the second lamb was to be sacrificed at twilight as a fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Describes the continual burnt offering at the entrance of the tent of meeting, where the Lord would meet with the people.
Refers to the first lamb that was to be offered in the morning, which the evening offering was to match.
Describes the grain offering and drink offering that were to accompany the burnt offering, which the evening offering also included.
Elijah sacrificed on Mount Carmel at the time of the evening offering, demonstrating the continued practice of the evening sacrifice.
Elijah stepped forward at the time of the grain offering (the evening offering), linking it to the daily sacrificial service.
Ezra bowed down in prayer at the time of the evening offering, illustrating the connection between the evening sacrifice and prayer.
Gabriel came to Daniel at the time of the evening offering, highlighting the spiritual significance of this moment.
Contrasts the repeated sacrifices with Christ's single sacrifice, which fulfilled what the daily offerings pointed toward.
